questions.question: A man decided to cover 7.5 km in 72 minutes. He decided to cover two thirds of the distance at 5 km/h and the remaining at some different speed. Find the speed after two third distance has been covered.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total distance = 7.5 km.

Time to cover the total distance = 72 minutes = 1.2 hours (since 72/60 = 1.2).

Speed for two thirds of the distance = 5 km/h.

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculation:**

Distance for two thirds = (2/3) × 7.5 km = 5 km.

Remaining distance = 7.5 km - 5 km = 2.5 km.

Time taken to cover two thirds of the distance = 5 km / 5 km/h = 1 hour.

Time left for the remaining distance = 1.2 hours - 1 hour = 0.2 hours.

Speed for the remaining distance = Distance / Time = 2.5 km / 0.2 hours = 12.5 km/h.

**The speed after two third distance has been covered is 12.5 km/h.**

questions.question: A boat is rowed down a river for 72 km in 9 hours and up a river for 42 km in some time. In how many hours will the boat be rowed up the river for 42 km, if the boat is running at an average speed of 7 km/h?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Downstream distance = 72 km

Downstream time = 9 hours

Upstream distance = 42 km

Average speed of boat = 7 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Speed downstream = Distance downstream / Time downstream

Speed downstream = 72 km / 9 hours

Speed downstream = 8 km/h

The speed of the stream = Speed downstream - Speed of boat

Speed of the stream = 8 km/h - 7 km/h

Speed of the stream = 1 km/h

Speed upstream = Speed of boat - Speed of the stream

Speed upstream = 7 km/h - 1 km/h

Speed upstream = 6 km/h

Time upstream = Distance upstream / Speed upstream

Time upstream = 42 km / 6 km/h

Time upstream = 7 hours

**The boat will be rowed up the river for 42 km in 7 hours.**

questions.question: In ΔABC, O is the point of intersection of the bisectors of ∠B and ∠A. If ∠BOC = 108°, then ∠BAO = ?

In ΔABC, if O is the intersection of angle bisectors, it is the incenter.

Property: ∠BOC = 90° + (∠A / 2)

Given ∠BOC = 108° ⇒ 108° = 90° + (∠A / 2) ⇒ ∠A / 2 = 18°

Since AO is the bisector of ∠A, ∠BAO = ∠A / 2 = 18°.

**∴ The correct answer is 18°.**

⇒ The angle subtended by a side at the incenter: ∠BOC = 90° + (∠A / 2)

⇒ 108° = 90° + (∠A / 2)

⇒ ∠A / 2 = 108° − 90°

questions.question: If P(A cup B)=(5)/(9), P(bar{A} cup bar{B})=(13)/(27), P(A)=(11)/(18), then the odds against the event B are:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find P(A ∩ B) using De Morgan Law: P(A ∩ B) = 1 − P(Ā ∪ B̄) = 1 − 13/27 = 14/27.

Calculate P(B) using Addition Rule: P(B) = P(A ∪ B) + P(A ∩ B) − P(A) = 5/9 + 14/27 − 11/18.

Using LCM 54: P(B) = (30 + 28 − 33) / 54 = 25/54.

Odds against B = P(B̄) : P(B) = (54 − 25) : 25 = 29 : 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 29/25.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P(A ∪ B) = 5/9

P(Ā ∪ B̄) = 13/27

P(A) = 11/18

**Formula Used:**

1. De Morgan's Law: P(Ā ∪ B̄) = P((A ∩ B)̄) = 1 − P(A ∩ B)

2. Addition Theorem: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)

3. Odds against event B = P(B̄) / P(B) = (1 − P(B)) / P(B)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d96a29162179eb17ebfa1bb8cefe906f52464e56aa526f418ae8d9ce63ab1154.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ P(A ∩ B) = 1 − P(Ā ∪ B̄)

⇒ P(A ∩ B) = 1 − 13/27 = 14/27

⇒ P(B) = P(A ∪ B) − P(A) + P(A ∩ B)

⇒ P(B) = 5/9 − 11/18 + 14/27

⇒ LCM of 9, 18, 27 is 54.

⇒ P(B) = (30 − 33 + 28) / 54 = 25/54

⇒ P(B̄) = 1 − 25/54 = 29/54

⇒ Odds against B = P(B̄) / P(B) = (29/54) / (25/54)

⇒ Odds against B = 29/25

**∴ The correct answer is 29/25.**

**__Additional Information__**

De Morgan's Laws

For any two events A and B, P(Ā ∩ B̄) = P((A ∪ B)̄) and P(Ā ∪ B̄) = P((A ∩ B)̄).

Odds in Favor vs Odds Against

Odds in favor of an event E are P(E) : P(Ē). Odds against an event E are P(Ē) : P(E).

Probability Addition Theorem

For any events A and B, P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). If they are mutually exclusive, P(A ∩ B) = 0.</p

questions.question: A discount of 10% is offered on the price of an article if the payment is made online. An additional discount of 5% is given to credit card holders. A person wishes to buy a watch priced at Rs. 60,000 by paying online through credit card. How much does he need to pay (in Rs.)?

Selling Price = 100% − 14.5% = 85.5% of Marked Price

Successive Discounts Formula

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the equivalent single discount is given by [a + b − (ab/100)]%.
